problems.source_says: The paper describes assessment of students’ writing samples, group pre/post means, paired t-tests and ANCOVA, but does not explicitly identify one observation in the writing analysis. It does not state the number of writing samples per student or how sample/rater scores were reduced to an analyzed score. A participant-level unit is plausible, but cannot be explicitly verified for any of the four outcomes; the confirmed unit is null. This is insufficient documentation, not evidence that another particular unit was used.
problems.quote: Within-group changes from pre- to post-test were examined using paired samples t-tests.
problems.locator: PDF p. 8 (journal p. 86), Section 3.3.1(c) and Section 3.6; PDF p. 11 (journal p. 89), RQ3; PDF p. 12 (journal p. 90), Figure 3. Full markdown and all 17 PDF pages searched for further unit/scoring information; codebook Section 6 defines unit as one observation in the paper’s analysis.

confirmed.statement: S1-O1 through S1-O4 concern scored writing output: the Creative Writing Assessment Rubric evaluates students’ writing samples for word usage, narrative structure and creativity, and RQ3 reports their total writing score. Criterion 3 holds.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 8 (journal p. 86), Section 3.3.1(c); PDF p. 11 (journal p. 89), RQ3; PDF p. 12 (journal p. 90), Figure 3.

confirmed.statement: All four outcomes correctly have ai_available_when_produced=no and question=after_ai: Figure 1 labels both tests Storytelling Task (No AI Help), with the post-test following the AI workshop/control period.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 6 (journal p. 84), Figure 1, visually inspected pre-test and post-test boxes and connecting arrows; codebook Section 1.

confirmed.statement: Immediate timing is supported: both groups received the instruments immediately before and after the five-week intervention.
S1-O1 overall_creativity matches the rubric’s Creativity dimension; no narrower novelty or cross-person diversity measure is specified.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 8 (journal p. 86), Section 3.3.1(c); PDF p. 12 (journal p. 90), Figure 3, Creativity bars; codebook Section 6.

confirmed.statement: S1-O2 other describes the total writing score spanning word usage, narrative structure and creativity; S1-O3 and S1-O4 usefulness represent narrative structure and word usage as output-quality dimensions.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 8 (journal p. 86), Section 3.3.1(c); PDF pp. 11-12 (journal pp. 89-90), RQ3 and Figure 3; codebook Section 6, other and usefulness definitions.

confirmed.statement: Leaving measure=null is supported: the paper names the assessment rubric but does not identify the scorer, scorer expertise, or an automated scoring method.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 8 (journal p. 86), Section 3.3.1(c); complete markdown reviewed, including references and author biography, with PDF text searched for scorer/rating details.

confirmed.statement: S1-O2 before_after reported values match exactly: experimental-group mean overall writing score increased from 3.34 to 8.71 out of 15.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 11 (journal p. 89), RQ3, first results paragraph; PDF p. 12 (journal p. 90), Figure 3 caption identifies the experimental group.

confirmed.statement: S1-O1, S1-O3 and S1-O4 before_after directions and figure_only descriptions match Figure 3: each post-test bar exceeds its pre-test bar, without numerical bar labels or uncertainty bars.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 12 (journal p. 90), Figure 3, visually inspected; PDF p. 11 (journal p. 89), RQ3 Findings states gains across writing dimensions without their exact means.

confirmed.statement: No numerical between-group writing estimate, control writing means, writing SDs, analyzed writing counts, test statistics, exact p-values, intervals or effect sizes are supplied. The reported p<.001 on the writing-results page belongs to writing anxiety; the form correctly leaves between-group writing direction unconfirmed.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 8 (journal p. 86), Section 3.6 describes analyses; PDF p. 11 (journal p. 89), RQ3; PDF p. 12 (journal p. 90), Figure 3. Complete results and discussion checked.

confirmed.statement: No additional qualifying output outcome was found: AI literacy and writing anxiety are questionnaire outcomes, and qualitative creativity/idea-expansion findings are interview perceptions. No scored comparison across different people’s outputs or scored workshop output with AI available is reported.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 7 (journal p. 85), Table 1 and Section 3.3.1(a-b); PDF p. 8 (journal p. 86), Section 3.3.2; PDF pp. 9-13 (journal pp. 87-91), RQ1-RQ4 and Figures 2-4; complete markdown read through journal p. 95, with no appendix present.

summary: The participant analysis unit is not explicitly supported for any of the four outcomes. Criterion 3 still holds because creativity is scored on unassisted writing samples, and the after_ai coding and reported total scores are supported.
